html:
The Bujang Valley in Kedah holds the remains of an ancient port and over fifty Hindu and Buddhist temples, the oldest known civilisation of the Malay Peninsula. Iron working at Sungai Batu dates back to the early centuries CE.

The port, known in Indian texts as Kadaram, traded with India, China and the Middle East, and later fell under the power of Srivijaya. In 1025 the Chola navy of south India raided it.

The sites faded as trade moved and Islam spread. Kedah's later sultans claim descent from its old kings. See also Hinduism and the Terengganu stone.
